subject: Re: DPA / No-adaptive-training commitment and subprocessor routing — evidence request
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthsync.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA question — no-adaptive-training, onshore processing proof

Hi Neha,

Hope you had a great weekend. We are finalizing our DPA review with legal & procurement and a couple of points came up we need clarified before we can sign:

1) HealthSync requires a no-adaptive-training commitment: we need confirmation that data sent to Redwood will not be used to improve or retrain any models (including internal research/ops pipelines) without explicit opt-in. A signed short affirmation would be ideal.

2) Subprocessors & routing: we need the current subprocessor list and evidence that for US customers data can be routed and processed only onshore (US) with customer-managed KMS options for key residency. If any subprocessors have cross-border processing, please note it.

3) Prompt/response ownership: Legal asked whether HealthSync retains rights to prompt/response content and any derivatives. We currently reference your standard DPA language but would prefer an explicit clause in the addendum.

Can you provide the above, and an example evidence pack (SOC2 plus subprocessor inventory) and an expected turnaround? We are aiming to close the PO this week.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Sr. Legal Ops | HealthSync

--

-Neha

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-02-15T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA question — no-adaptive-training, onshore processing proof

Emma / Neha — attaching our current subprocessor inventory and SOC2 Type II report (stubs referenced below). Notes:

- Subprocessors: the attached Subprocessor_List_2027-02.pdf lists infra, telemetry, and storage vendors. For HealthSync we can gate routing policies so customer traffic is processed on Redwood US regions only (us-east-1 / us-west-2) and we can enforce onshore-only compute via project routing rules.

- KMS options: we offer a customer-provided KMS integration (bring-your-own) for encryption at rest key binding. Keys can be provisioned in your AWS account (supported policies documented). This satisfies onshore key residency when keys are in a US region.

- Cross-border subprocessors: a small subset of telemetry vendors operate globally; however, we do not send prompt/response payloads to external telemetry processors by default — only aggregate telemetry. Where customers require strict onshore processing, we will disable telemetry exports and route logs through our onshore-only pipeline.

Attachments (stubs in this thread):
- Subprocessor_List_2027-02.pdf (inventory + country processing notes)
- SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (redacted)

Let me know if you need a signed subprocessor attestation.

-DK
David Kim
Director, Infrastructure & Platform — Redwood Inference

2) For the customer-provided KMS pattern, can you share the IAM policy template or runbook that shows which roles need access? We need that to scope our security review.

Emma
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthsync.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-15T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA question — no-adaptive-training, onshore processing proof

Emma — below is the proposed affirmation language and prompt/response addendum wording. Happy to refine but this is what we can sign immediately:

Affirmation (one-paragraph, signable):
"Redwood Inference affirms that, with respect to HealthSync (Customer), Customer-provided content (including prompts and model responses) will not be used to improve, adapt, or retrain any production or research model used to serve the Customer, except where Customer has provided explicit written consent. Redwood will only retain prompt/response data for debugging and SLO monitoring for a maximum of 30 days unless otherwise agreed in writing; such retained data will not be used for model training or improvement."

Proposed addendum clause (for inclusion in DPA):
"Customer retains ownership of prompts and generated responses and grants Redwood a limited service right to process such content solely to provide the agreed inference service. Redwood will not assert derivative ownership over Customer content or outputs and will not use Customer content to train models absent Customer's explicit written opt-in."

Operational items:
- Telemetry flag: set `export.raw_prompts=false` at project-level for your account; David can provide the exact API call and permissions.
- KMS runbook: David will attach the IAM example.

If these read ok, I can produce a DocuSign package (affirmation + DPA addendum) and share it — estimated turnaround < 24 hours once you confirm.

-S
Sean Gallagher
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
